text:
Maya: heads-up — after yesterday's runtime change the qwen2.5 p99 for short-chat (<=64 tokens) spiked ~45%. Seen across dedicated and hosted canaries, not universal though.
Igor: do you have a perf trace? is this only with kernel auto-select enabled? which quant/compile path?
Maya: collecting traces now. quick numbers from last canary: baseline p50 18ms p95 46ms p99 82ms; after bump p50 20ms p95 78ms p99 122ms. tokens/sec dropped ~30% local. nvprof shows more small kernels firing and poor SM occupancy.
Maya: sample profile snippet:
```
kernel k-attn-v2 launch 48x... time 0.12ms (many calls)
kernel matmul-fused-16 time 0.9ms (less efficient for s=32)
kv-cache-copy time 0.05ms (hot path)
concurrent-launches spiked 3x
```
Anika: hmm that sounds like the auto-kernel heuristic prefers the fused matmul for >32 heads, but qwen2.5 has nonstandard head/kv dims and small seqs -> kernel thrash. try forcing k-attn-v2 for seq<=64 and heads>=32.
Sam: +1 also look at batching window heuristics — the new heuristic increased max batch latency to 8ms to gather tokens; that helps throughput but kills p99 for short queries. I recommend 3-4ms for chat workloads.
Igor: there's also a KV layout mismatch reported last week on the Qwen tokenizer multi-lang runs: some tokenizers emit longer token runs for mixed CJK+arabic sequences, causing a kv-head offset drift in our index calc. if the kernel assumes contiguous KV layout for head dims it's going to mis-index and cause micro-copies.
Maya: we saw a tiny but consistent extra memcpy in the traces tied to kv index calculation. repro: send mixed zh+ar prompt, seq ~40, get an extra memcpy per layer.
Anika: can you drop a quick config we used? i'll try a manual rollback of the kernel selector + turn off ALiBi fallback to pure RoPE path and rerun canary.
Maya: test config we deployed (excerpt):
```
serving.runtime.autokernel: true
serving.runtime.max_batch_latency_ms: 8
rope.scaling.strategy: auto
attention.variant.fallback: alibi,rope
```
Anika: try this patch locally:
```
serving.runtime.autokernel: false
serving.runtime.preferred_kernel: "k-attn-v2"
serving.runtime.max_batch_latency_ms: 4
rope.scaling.strategy: "fixed:1.0"
attention.variant.fallback: "rope_only"
```
Sam: also instrument a per-request kv-head-dim sanity check in dev build, log if head_dim != kv_dim *or* calculated offsets would overflow buffer. Keep it off in prod but enables quick bisect.
Maya: ran anika's patch on a small canary: p99 dropped back to ~85ms (close to baseline), tokens/sec recovered to ~95% of baseline. no extra memcpy in trace. good sign.
Igor: great. do we have a hypothesis why autokernel picked the worse path? maybe heuristic weights changed when we added multilang tokenizer cost in the model profile. it might have bumped the cost estimate for k-attn-v2 incorrectly.
Anika: yes the new cost model adds a "tokenizer-penalty" to prefer fewer launches for long-token models — that penalized short seq paths inadvertently. need to separate tokenizer-cost from kernel selection and feed seq-length distribution instead.
Ryan: can we add a quick canary plan: roll kernel-autoselect rollback in hosted for 10% traffic, keep dedicated untouched, monitor p99/throughput, enable per-request kv-sanity logging at 1% sample.
deploy-bot: scheduled canary: hosted 10% @ 2026-03-18T11:40Z. Auto-rollback on p99>baseline+25% for 5min.
Maya: started canary at 1899915200. initial 10-minute window looks stable. leaving it for 30.
Anika: next steps: 1) revert the tokenizer-penalty in cost model (separate PR), 2) add kernel selectors that consider head/kv dim mismatch, 3) add quick runtime guard for kv indexing and sampled logging, 4) tune batching window for chat workloads (3-4ms). I'll file PRs.
Sam: filing an incident-lite doc with perf numbers + repro (multilang mixed CJK+Arabic) and the rollback steps. attach nvprof traces and config diffs.
Maya: thx all. marking this thread resolved after full rollback and PRs merged.
deploy-bot: canary completed at 1899915600 — rollout healthy. :white_check_mark:
Ryan: closing loop — will follow up if the tokenizer cost model change needs more fine-grained telemetry.
